newsitem.title: UK: Tesco dips, BZW wary on industry margins.
newsitem.headline: Tesco dips, BZW wary on industry margins.

text.p: Shares in supermarket group Tesco Plc dropped in a rising market on Wednesday after investors digested Tuesday's results, with analysts warning that margins were set to tighten and competition to intensify.
The shares were off 3p at 361p by 1038 GMT, after adding 11-1/2p yesterday in response to the company's results for the year through February.

Other supermarket stocks were also weak with Safeway Plc down 2p at 367, J. Sainsbury Plc down 1p at 327 and ASDA Group Plc down 1/2p at 111-1/2. By contrast the FTSE 100 index was up 21.8 points at 4,291.1.
Tesco reported a ten percent rise in pre-tax profits to 750 million stg, and added that gross margins were expected to stabilise.
But the Financial Times' Lex column commented on Wednesday that the outlook for the industry was not as rosy as the market's reaction had suggested.
David McCarthy, industry analyst at BZW, agreed that the environment was one of tightening margins and further competitive pressure.
"Petrol margins have bounced to the tune of 35 million (stg), so if you strip them out, non-petrol margins must be falling," he said.

"Tesco is also a bigger company this year, it has better buying power and (store) extensions which are higher gross margin areas. The competition does not have these advantages so their margins look set to fall," McCarthy said.
The FT commented that in a flat margin environment Tesco was likely to be pushing agressively for sales growth.
"Tesco's success may not be dependent on failure elsewhere...but their strategy may well cause it," McCarthy said.
J. Sainsbury Plc is seen as the most vulnerable to Tesco's recent success.
"They will have serious problems," said the analyst. "They have to adjust to a competitor who has become 30-40 percent bigger than themselves."
BZW has a "hold" rating on Tesco and views the stock as a long-term winner, together with Safeway. ASDA is seen as a potential underperformer at BZW.
